notes: Independently reviewed all 20 production TypeScript files and both package/manifest metadata files. The 47-file plugin inventory is partitioned into 22 reviewed and 25 excluded files; source bytes were checked against the pinned commit.

provider.test-support.ts was individually read and excluded only after verifying its two callers are index.test.ts and auth-reconnect.test.ts. It imports Vitest and the SDK test API; these test-only dependencies do not enter production expectations.

Every production relative import remains within extensions/github-copilot. api.ts reexports the plugin-owned domain helper; register.runtime.ts reexports plugin-owned runtime-auth, starter-model, and usage helpers. Their dynamic imports do not create SDK dynamic-import or reexport findings. There is no additional shared shipped source outside this root.

All 22 imported SDK subpaths are exact public package.json exports; their source facades establish the named exports. Public export names remain canonical, including provider-auth#upsertAuthProfileWithLock, whose SDK facade aliases its internal Compat implementation. SDK implementations and separately installed packages are not recursively attributed.

The definePluginEntry register callback proves exactly api.registerEmbeddingProvider and api.registerProvider. ProviderAuthContext, provider/catalog/model callback contexts, OAuth callbacks, embedding adapter options, and the plugin-owned objects named runtime or runtimeAuth are not OpenClawPluginApi or PluginRuntime handles. Their properties do not create API/runtime findings.

Provider methods such as prepareDynamicModel, buildReplayPolicy, wrapStreamFn, and fetchUsageSnapshot are provider contracts, not named API on/registerHook registrations. There are no named hook or runtime-member findings.

Explicit import type and inline type imports remain type dependencies with representative annotation/indexed-access evidence. Indexed access on provider model/context types is not public API/runtime indexed access. No ordinary value import is reclassified based on hypothetical emitted JavaScript.

Known SDK helper calls retain their direct exported-function dependencies without inferring internal API/runtime consumption. Calls on arbitrary helper return values (such as fetch release callbacks) are not SDK-export or runtime-member calls.

The manifest contributes providers plus contracts.embeddingProviders and contracts.usageProviders. Model catalog rows, provider endpoints/request policy, auth/setup choices, CLI option descriptions, category, and config schema are metadata outside the agreed contract identities.
